correctness.rationale: On a full block the sampling weight is (2m−1)/T², and conditional on m the shift is the uniform grid of mesh 1/(2m−1). The weighted bounded-Lipschitz grid error is O(1/T) even after multiplication by bounded statistics of m. Divisor factorization gives log D(m²)=log(3/2)ω(m)+H(m). Fixed bounded valuation patterns are congruence conditions; CRT gives their weighted geometric probabilities. For Erdős–Kac in a fixed class, truncate at T^(1/log log T) excluding primes dividing the modulus: CRT gives each fixed joint moment the independent-prime main term with total error T^(−1+o(1)), and the omitted primes have conditional mean O_q(1+log log log T) by Mertens and summing the counting errors. For each fixed lower-scale endpoint tT, the same normalized Gaussian law holds since replacing log log T by log log(tT) is negligible; partial summation gives it under the root weight. Thus the normalized ω is asymptotically independent of each finite valuation vector, not just marginally Gaussian. The weighted expectation of the discarded correction above B is bounded by 2 sum_(p>B)1/[p(p−1)]. This makes the correction tight, permits the finite-prime product limit and Slutsky replacement, and implies almost-sure finite support in primes in the model. The remaining incomplete block has O(1/T) mass. The zero and smallest positive atoms follow respectively from all valuations ≤1 and exactly one valuation equal to 2. A fresh rational enclosure (/workspace/branches/7b2beb61-f14c-4930-ace9-73fec79f60fd/atom_certificate.py) bounds the latter probability between 0.2007556808 and 0.2007562888, sufficient for the displayed rounding; it is a numerical check, not the limiting-law proof. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed.
